subject: Economics
description: GDP / GNP / NDP / NNP / NI / PI / DPI; nominal vs real; methods of estimation

questions.stem: GDP at MARKET PRICE differs from GDP at FACTOR COST by:

options.option_text: Net foreign income from abroad to residents
Net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies)
Depreciation of capital stock during the year
Inflation rate of the country in that period

questions.explanation: GDP at MARKET PRICE = GDP at FACTOR COST + (Indirect Taxes − Subsidies) = GDP at FC + NET INDIRECT TAXES. Market price includes taxes (paid by buyer); factor cost reflects what producers actually receive. India officially uses GVA (Gross Value Added) at basic prices = GDP at FC since 2015 (CSO methodology revision). Distractor 1 = difference between GDP and GNP (NFIA). Distractor 3 = difference between gross + net (depreciation). Distractor 4 = nominal vs real adjustment.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: GNP differs from GDP by which adjustment?

options.option_text: Subtracting depreciation from gross value
Adding net factor income from abroad (NFIA)
Adding all indirect taxes minus subsidies
Multiplying by current inflation rate level

questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + NFIA. NFIA = factor income earned by Indians abroad − factor income earned by foreigners in India. GDP is TERRITORIAL (within India's borders); GNP is NATIONAL (Indians anywhere). For India, NFIA is usually slightly NEGATIVE (we're a net debtor; pay more interest abroad than we earn) → GNP slightly < GDP. NDP = GDP − depreciation. NNP = GNP − depreciation. NI (National Income) = NNP at factor cost.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: REAL GDP differs from NOMINAL GDP because Real GDP:

options.option_text: Includes net factor income from abroad too
Adjusts for inflation using a base-year price
Is always larger than the nominal GDP value
Is calculated only by central planning bodies

questions.explanation: NOMINAL GDP — at current-year prices. REAL GDP — at base-year prices (CONSTANT PRICES). Adjusts for inflation to show genuine production change. India base year: 2011-12 (will be revised to 2022-23 around 2025-26). Real growth = (Nominal growth − Inflation) approximately. GDP DEFLATOR = (Nominal/Real) × 100 → broad price-level measure. Comparing 2024 GDP to 1990 GDP only meaningful in REAL terms. During inflation, nominal > real.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: PER CAPITA INCOME of a country is calculated as:

options.option_text: GDP divided by total area of the country
National Income divided by total population
Total tax revenue divided by population
Imports plus exports divided by population

questions.explanation: Per Capita Income = National Income / Population. India's per capita income (FY24): ~₹2.13 lakh (~$2,500). World average: ~$13,000. Per capita gives a sense of average prosperity but hides inequality. INDIA's per capita is much lower than China's (~$13,000), Bangladesh's ($2,800 — recently overtook India in some years). Income inequality measured by GINI coefficient (0 = perfect equality, 1 = max inequality). Distractor 1 = density-related concept. Distractors 3, 4 are unrelated.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The first SCIENTIFIC ESTIMATE of national income for India was made by:

options.option_text: Mahalanobis at the Indian Statistical Institute
Dadabhai Naoroji, in his 1867-68 estimates
VKRV Rao, in his 1925 doctoral thesis
Indian National Income Committee in 1949

questions.explanation: DADABHAI NAOROJI — first to estimate India's national income (1867-68; in his 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', 1901). Estimated per capita income ~₹20/year. Pioneered the 'DRAIN THEORY' — colonial drain of Indian wealth to Britain. Other key contributors: William Digby (1899), Findlay Shirras (1911), VKRV Rao (1925-29 — produced the first systematic study), Wadia + Joshi. Post-independence, the National Income Committee (1949, chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis) put national income estimation on a scientific basis. CSO (Central Statistics Office, now NSO) handles current estimates.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The PRIMARY SECTOR in national income accounting refers to:

options.option_text: Manufacturing industries and construction sectors
Agriculture, fishing, forestry, mining (raw extraction)
Banking, insurance, IT services and trade
Government welfare-spending and subsidy schemes

questions.explanation: Three-sector classification (Clark, Fisher): PRIMARY = extraction of raw materials from nature (agriculture, fishing, forestry, mining, quarrying). SECONDARY = manufacturing, construction, electricity (transformation of raw materials). TERTIARY = services (trade, transport, banking, IT, hospitality, government). India's GVA share (FY24): primary ~17%, secondary ~28%, tertiary ~55%. Trend — India is becoming services-led without going through full industrialisation (unusual development path; some call it 'premature deindustrialisation').
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Three METHODS of measuring national income are:

options.option_text: Direct, indirect and via household surveys
Production (value-added), Income, and Expenditure
Random sampling, full census and modelling
Top-down, bottom-up and meta-aggregation

questions.explanation: Three EQUIVALENT methods (yielding same result in theory): (1) PRODUCTION / VALUE-ADDED method — sum of Gross Value Added across all sectors; avoids double-counting by counting only value added at each stage. (2) INCOME method — sum of factor incomes (wages + rent + interest + profit) earned by residents. (3) EXPENDITURE method — sum of final demand: C + I + G + (X−M) (consumption + investment + govt. + net exports). India uses combination — value-added for production estimates, expenditure as cross-check. CSO publishes via all three. Discrepancies adjusted in final accounts.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which of the following payments is EXCLUDED from GDP because it does not correspond to any current productive service rendered?

options.option_text: Government salaries paid to active civil servants for services rendered
Old-age pension disbursed by the government to retired employees
Interest earned by banks on loans extended to private businesses
Rent received by landlords for leasing commercial office space

questions.explanation: Pensions are transfer payments — money moves from government to retirees without any current productive service in return, so they are excluded from GDP. Government salaries, bank interest income, and rent are all payments for current factor services (labour, capital, land) and ARE included in GDP.

questions.stem: Which single deduction transforms Gross National Product (GNP) into Net National Product (NNP)?

options.option_text: Net factor income from abroad earned by resident nationals
Capital consumption allowance, also known as depreciation
Net indirect taxes comprising indirect taxes minus subsidies paid
Value of intermediate goods consumed during the production process

questions.explanation: NNP = GNP − Depreciation (Capital Consumption Allowance), which accounts for wear and tear of capital assets. Net factor income from abroad is the adjustment used to convert GDP → GNP, not GNP → NNP. Net indirect taxes convert market-price aggregates to factor-cost aggregates — a separate dimension entirely.

questions.stem: The 'value-added method' of measuring national income was introduced specifically to overcome which inherent problem in the gross output method?

options.option_text: Inability to capture imputed value of owner-occupied housing stock
Risk of counting intermediate goods multiple times as final output
Difficulty separating nominal output from real output at current prices
Challenge of including informal sector transactions in official estimates

questions.explanation: The value-added method counts only the incremental value added at each production stage (Output − Intermediate inputs), eliminating double-counting. Without it, steel used to make a car would be counted twice — once as steel output and again embedded in the car's value. Imputed rent, nominal vs real, and informal sector are separate problems requiring different solutions.

questions.stem: Personal Disposable Income (PDI) is derived from Personal Income (PI) by deducting which specific item?

options.option_text: Undistributed profits retained by corporations from their net earnings
Direct personal taxes and compulsory non-tax payments to government
Net factor income earned by residents from assets placed abroad
Social security contributions paid by employers on behalf of workers

questions.explanation: PDI = PI − Direct Personal Taxes − Non-Tax Payments (fines, compulsory fees). This is what households actually have available to spend or save. Undistributed corporate profits are deducted at an earlier stage (moving from NNP to Personal Income, not PI to PDI). Social security contributions by employers are also excluded before arriving at PI.

questions.stem: Among the following, which non-monetary item is conventionally INCLUDED in India's national income estimates as per standard accounting norms?

options.option_text: Domestic services performed by housewives within their own households
Imputed rental value of houses occupied by their respective owners
Voluntary services rendered by NGO workers without any remuneration
Value of barter transactions conducted in rural informal economies

questions.explanation: Imputed rent of owner-occupied houses is included because the owner implicitly receives rental income equal to what a tenant would pay — excluding it would understate housing services in GDP. Domestic housework, volunteer NGO labour, and most barter exchanges are excluded because they lack observable market prices and are difficult to measure consistently.

questions.stem: A country's GDP at market price is ₹500 lakh crore, depreciation is ₹40 lakh crore, net indirect taxes are ₹60 lakh crore, and net factor income from abroad is ₹(−10) lakh crore. What is NNP at Factor Cost?

options.option_text: ₹400 lakh crore — arrived at by ignoring net factor income from abroad
₹390 lakh crore — obtained after applying all four adjustments correctly
₹460 lakh crore — obtained by deducting only depreciation and ignoring rest
₹410 lakh crore — computed by treating net factor income as a positive inflow

questions.explanation: NNP at FC = GDP at MP − Depreciation − Net Indirect Taxes + NFIA = 500 − 40 − 60 + (−10) = 390. Option A (₹400) omits NFIA entirely. Option C (₹460) deducts only depreciation: 500 − 40 = 460. Option D (₹410) incorrectly treats NFIA as positive: 500 − 40 − 60 + 10 = 410. The sign of NFIA is a common trap — a negative value means factor outflows exceed inflows.

questions.stem: When India's national accounts were rebased to the 2011-12 base year (released January 2015), what was the most notable CONCEPTUAL shift from the earlier 2004-05 series?

options.option_text: Gross Value Added at basic prices replaced GDP at factor cost as primary aggregate
MCA-21 corporate database replaced census surveys as the main data source
Real GDP growth replaced nominal GDP growth as India's official headline indicator
GDP at purchasing power parity replaced GDP at market exchange rates in reporting

questions.explanation: The 2011-12 series adopted 'GVA at basic prices' as the primary aggregate replacing 'GDP at factor cost'. Basic prices = factor cost + production taxes − production subsidies, making it a distinct concept. MCA-21 was a significant data-source change, not a conceptual one. Real GDP growth was already India's headline indicator before 2015. PPP-based GDP was never adopted as a replacement for market-exchange-rate reporting in India's official accounts.
